newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: SOCCER-ROBSON'S FUTURE UNCERTAIN DESPITE CUP WIN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ROBSON'S FUTURE UNCERTAIN DESPITE CUP WIN.

text.p: Despite Barcelona's triumph in the European Cup Winnners' Cup final over Paris St Germain on Wednesday, the future of coach Bobby Robson still rests in the balance.
But the 64-year-old Engishman hopes the 1-0 victory over the French side will help him see out the second year of his two season contract.
"People must judge me on my results. They have to think about just that.....There aren't too many presidents that get given the European Cup Winners' Cup trophy," he said.
"I came here for two years and I always thought I would be here two years," he added.
But he would not be drawn any further about his chances of staying at the Catalan club.
"You'd have to ask that to the president," he said.
Robson's tenure at Barcelona, not yet a season old, has looked shaky ever since arch rivals Real Madrid drew away from the Catalan club in the league.

Ajax Amsterdam coach Louis van Gaal has been strongly linked with Barcelona since he announced mid-season that he would be leaving Ajax this summer. Last month, Barcelona president Josep Lluis Nunez even went so far as to name van Gaal as next season's manager.

However, Robson dismissed talk of his early demise, saying he has already set himself a challenge for next season. Although Robson was not hopeful of overtaking Real, he said Barcelona would almost certainly qualify for the Champions League as the Spanish league's second-placed team. And Robson said he is the man to lead the team.
"Barcelona actually have the chance to lift the European Cup... a good chance. I'd like to think I would have a chance to be there," he said.
Robson has a chance to steer Barcelona to four trophies this season -- the Spanish title, Spanish Cup, and the Spanish Super Cup and European Cup Winners Cup which they have already secured.
But the internal politics at the Camp Nou could yet drive him out.

Passion was running deeply among the Barcelona fans on Wednesday. Although they saw their team win the European Cup in 1992, they remembered losing to AC Milan 4-0 in that competition in 1994 and also losing in the final of this cup in 1991.

Guardiola, who played a key role in Wednesday's victory, said: "I dedicate this win to the fans who saw us lose those matches. I wish I could cut my medal in half and present one part of it to the fans for those defeats."
Barcelona skipper Ghoerghe Popescu, who was substituted at half-time said: "My hamstring started to seize up after half an hour and I could not continue. But we did very well as a team tonight.
"We knew PSG would be hard to beat and they were. We had no particular tactics to beat them, you can't play like that in a cup final. But we deserved the victory for the way we played."
